root_idea.summary: A root centered on weakness, fatigue, and weariness.
root_idea.development: The core sense of weakness and fatigue extends to weakness of judgment, causes and experiences of tiring, and Classical technical uses for defective or disordered arrow-feathering.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A Quran-attested nominal form with an independently supported lexical meaning of fatigue or weariness.

senses.usage_conditions: A noun for the state of being tired or worn out; Quran translations may render it as “weariness,” “fatigue,” or “exhaustion.”

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal expressions for weakness or stupidity, distinct from the noun لُغُوب meaning fatigue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A weak or stupid person, especially one weak in judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person characterized by weakness of understanding or judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spoil or mar another’s affair, scheme, plan, or the like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with عَلَيْهِمْ and an understood affair, plan, or similar object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak ill or corruptly to people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal construction describing faulty or bad discourse addressed to others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a dog, to lap or drink by lapping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use with a dog as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To load a beast beyond what it can bear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II construction with a beast of carriage as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fatigue, tire, or weary someone severely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may also be a journey or travel that causes someone severe fatigue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an arrow’s feathers into the arrangement called لُغَاب.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The arrangement is the defective or uneven feathering described under لَغْبٌ and لُغَابٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, disordered, uneven, or incongruous arrow-feathers; also an arrow badly trimmed or made, including one that does not fly far.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of defective feather arrangement, contrasted with well-matched feathering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To chase, hunt, or pursue for a long time.
To undertake the management of something and carry it through successfully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction conveys that the person was not unequal to the task.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find a beast of carriage fatigued or exhausted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V construction describing the discovery of the beast’s fatigued state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corrupt, faulty, or ill-directed speech or discourse; evil or foul expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical nominal use for discourse that is bad, corrupt, or improperly directed.
An idiomatic expression with the neck as part of the phrase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flesh between the four front teeth, or incisors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun referring to the interstitial flesh between the front teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Languid or slack, said of winds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical use applied to winds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of fatigue, tiring, or weariness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for something that imposes fatigue; its plural is مَلَاغِبُ.
